role: a radiology / biomedical-imaging researcher analyzing small 3D CT volume crops of anatomical structures
subject: a 64^3-voxel CT volume crop of an anatomical structure (a lung nodule, an abdominal/thoracic organ, or a rib segment) from clinical CT, drawn from the MedMNIST v2 3D benchmarks (NoduleMNIST3D, OrganMNIST3D, FractureMNIST3D)
property: which MedMNIST3D subset the crop comes from (nodule / organ / fracture) and its ground-truth clinical label: nodule benign vs malignant; organ identity (one of 11 organs); rib-fracture category (buckle / nondisplaced / displaced)
request: These are 1496 individual 64x64x64-voxel CT volume crops from three MedMNIST v2 3D subsets: 500 lung nodules labelled benign/malignant, 495 organ crops spanning 11 organ classes, and 501 rib-segment crops labelled by fracture type. Find a concrete, novel, testable question these 3D volumes can answer, decide your own method, run real code on the volumes, and produce a short publishable paper.

_demo.selection: 2 nodule, 2 organ, and 3 fracture volumes with distinct labels
_demo.purpose: interface and perception smoke test; not the full paper evaluation
